expected: T004 F02-AC-014 requires rejected candidate bodies to never become executable durable artifacts. admitBlueprint must admit only one stable validator-issued PASSED snapshot whose report/admissible pair cannot change between provenance verification and repository persistence.
actual: Post-closure exhaustive audit found a TOCTOU admission bypass in the merged T004 implementation. admitBlueprint reads caller-owned result.admissible/result.report multiple times. A getter/Proxy can return a genuine sealed PASSED report+admissible pair for isSealedPassedResult(), then return a forged PASSED report plus rejected-body admissible object on later reads. The repository then sees run.status=PASSED and run.blueprint_hash matching the forged content_hash and can persist a body that was never validator-issued. Deep-freezing the genuine sealed pair does not stop the outer result object from changing which pair it returns. Same-class pre-reexecution audit also found that sealPassedResult itself is exported from admissible-provenance.ts. Any in-repo caller can construct an arbitrary PASSED report + arbitrary AdmissibleBlueprint, call the exported sealer, and thereby mint a WeakMap provenance pair accepted by admitBlueprint without passing validateBlueprintCandidate. The current provenance mechanism therefore has both a selection-TOCTOU flaw and an issuance-authority flaw.
evidence: Merged T004 implementation PR #188 source HEAD 89e078c2758a5f77a66bfa9d5da9a55596dc4e6f; canonical implementation merge 1918980b269fb11c11e386dd72d83bc7c5029003.

src/platform/blueprint/blueprint-admission.ts reads result.admissible for the rejected/PASSED branch, then reads result.report and result.admissible again for isSealedPassedResult(), then reads result.report again for runRecord(), then destructures result.admissible again before repository persistence.

Deterministic exploit order: admissible getter read #1 -> genuine sealed admissible; report getter #1 + admissible getter #2 -> genuine sealed pair passes WeakMap provenance; report getter #2 -> forged PASSED report; admissible getter #3 -> forged rejected-body content. PostgresBlueprintAdmissionRepository only requires PASSED + run.blueprint_hash === content.content_hash before executing admission.

admissible-provenance.ts deep-freezes the validator-issued report/admissible graph and binds exact admissible identity to exact report identity, but that invariant is checked only against one transient getter result and is not snapshotted for subsequent persistence reads.
Existing T004 forged-result regression cases use stable plain objects and therefore do not exercise accessor/Proxy identity switching after provenance verification.

This finding is implementation-only: BS-P1-012 already fixes the required semantics (only admitted validated Blueprint may become durable/executable; rejected candidate body must not). No Product/Schema decision is needed.

Prior T004 closure/evidence review is invalidated as sufficient closure proof by this post-closure counterexample. Existing EV-SP-P1-002-T004-001..010 remain historical records of the earlier green candidate/gates but must not be treated as sufficient completion evidence for final closure.

Fresh execution independently re-hashes body and checks schema/registry metadata. No additional T004 blocker found in this class.

Degradation audit reconfirmed F02-AC-015/016 boundaries: explicit degradation metadata is part of canonical/durable content, FULLY_SUPPORTED cannot hide degradations, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED cannot omit them, refs are exact/eligible, and preserves_semantic_core=false rejects before admission. F02 intentionally does not claim to semantically prove the natural-language Intent itself.

Rejected/INCOMPATIBLE report provenance is not currently sealed like PASSED provenance. An internal caller could fabricate/mutate validation_run evidence, but without a validator-issued admissible pair it still cannot create blueprint_content or executable durable content. This is explicitly classified as a T005 evidence/trace preflight obligation, not a T004 AC-013/014 closure blocker; T004 BF-041 remediation must nevertheless prove hostile rejected-result shapes never cause a body write.

Same-class seal-authority audit on canonical main 94aa544eeea8694c4292a1b3db2b67ae660c48fb: src/platform/blueprint/admissible-provenance.ts exports sealPassedResult(result), while repository-wide src scan shows validate-blueprint.ts is the only legitimate issuer and blueprint-admission.ts only needs verification.

Direct-seal counterexample: construct a PASSED report whose content_hash matches arbitrary canonical content, construct matching AdmissibleBlueprint, call exported sealPassedResult(), then pass the returned pair to admitBlueprint(); the current isSealedPassedResult WeakMap check succeeds because the public sealer itself enrolled the forged pair.

Final same-class audit classification: direct repository invocation and injectable validation Registry/runtime context are trusted-internal boundaries with no parallel production src caller and remain outside T004; POI-005 must later prove public wiring does not map client input into those trusted contexts. No third T004 blocker was found.

Closure-prep conclusion: after fixing both caller-owned result TOCTOU and provenance issuance authority, retaining the existing deep-freeze + identity check, and passing the full negative matrix, no additional known T004 AC-013..016 blocker remains.
